title: Cadence Anchorplay Lab — Prompt Cadence & Anchor Experiments
content:
Objective:
- Explore how temporal "cadence" (spacing and repetition of anchor/instruction frames) affects instruction fidelity and hallucination risk in few-shot templates.
- Produce compact heuristics for using anchors (short framing sentences, example separators, token markers) so downstream apps can balance token budget vs instruction stability.

Quick summary of intuition so far:
- Frequent, brief anchors (1–2 tokenized sentences repeated every 3–5 turns) keep role fidelity high but increase token cost and occasionally provoke repeaty output.
- Sparse anchors (anchor once at start) reduce cost but risk drift after ~1200 tokens for current model family (observed on open-Large-v2).
- Interleaving exemplar shots with micro-anchors (a one-line directive inserted between examples) seems to improve consistency with little cost.

Experimental setup notes (informal):
- Model: open-Large-v2 (test bed), temp=0.2 / 0.6 / 1.0, max_tokens=512, top_p sweeps.
- Prompt envelope: [SYSTEM ANCHOR] + [FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES] + [USER QUERY].
- Metrics collected: instruction adherence (binary judged), hallucination tokens (manual count), repetition ratio, length-to-quality tradeoff (qualitative).
- Run names: cadence-A (anchor every 1), cadence-B (anchor once), cadence-C (micro-anchor between shots).

Concrete few-shot templates used (kept minimal to save tokens):

Shot format (compact):
- <role>=Assistant | <goal>=summarize email thread into 3 bullets | <style>=concise

Few-shot set (3 exemplars):
EX1:
User: "Important: summarize and list action items for the thread below. Mention only owners and deadlines."
Assistant: "3 bullets: 1) Owner - deadline - action; 2) ..."

EX2:
User: "TL;DR plus next step suggestion (one sentence)."
Assistant: "Summary in one line. Next step: assign to X by DATE."

EX3:
User: "Produce a short subject line and 2 bullet next actions."
Assistant: "Subject: ...
- Action 1: ...
- Action 2: ..."

Anchor variants tested (phrases):
- Anchor long: "You are a very concise summarizer. Provide only owners and deadlines when asked."
- Anchor short: "Concise summarizer: owners & deadlines only."
- Token marker: "---ANCHOR---" followed by a 6-10 token instruction.

Failure cases observed (notes to self):
- Drift after ~900 tokens in cadence-B: model starts to invent owners (generic names) even when example format is strict.
- Anchor-triggered repetition: cadence-A increased repeated phrases like "Action:" across bullets (style overfit).
- Micro-anchor misalignment: when micro-anchor placed immediately after a counterexample (bad shot), the model prioritized the bad shot's style. Need to control shot quality.
- Temperature sensitivity: high temp + sparse anchors => nonsense next-step suggestions, sometimes contradictory to examples.

Small adversarial cases I tried (copy raw):
- Query: "Summarize and assign: thread below. The thread contains "Alice says she'll do it" but also a later line says "no one assigned". Make up the owner if unclear."
- Result: model sometimes chooses to "make up" a plausible owner when anchor sparse. With stronger anchor phrasing (explicit forbid making up), hallucinations drop but terse anchors get ignored after long dialog context.

Notes on separators and layout: 
- Using explicit separators ("---") between shots reduced cross-shot bleeding for cadences A/B by ~10% in our small sample.
- Numbering examples (EX1/EX2) helped the model map patterns to expected response format.

Heuristic draft (working):
- For short-live sessions (<800 tokens): prefer single anchor + 2 exemplars.
- For long sessions (>800 tokens) or multi-turn assistants: repeat a micro-anchor every 4 user turns.
- When token budget is tight: convert anchors to token markers and allow model to reference previous inline exemplar by index ("use EX2 style").
- Always include an explicit prohibition line if hallucination is critical: "Do not invent owners; if unknown, say 'unknown'." Put that in the anchor and in last exemplar.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How does cadence interact with model size/quantization? (run quick matrix on small/med/lg)
- Automate selection of anchor frequency given observed token window and request latency SLA. Could be a console recommendation.
- Test with role-played personas (long persona text repeated vs short token anchor). Which is cheaper for stability?
- Evaluate with Redwood "Optimize" suggestions (quantization + anchor frequency) — file a follow-up ticket.

Mini checklist for next session:
- [ ] Run cadence matrix for temp=0.2/0.6 on med model (3 runs each).
- [ ] Add a control with explicit "do not invent" prohibition inside exemplar only (no separate anchor).
- [ ] Sample 50 real emails from CS sandbox and run human eval for instruction adherence.

Scratch fragments (untidy):
- "anchor-as-index" idea: store exemplar signatures in KV and reference by short token (EX2#). Could save tokens but needs runtime support for KV lookups.
- "soft anchor": change phrasing over time (synonyms) to avoid repetition-triggered overfitting. Curious if it reduces repeated phrase hallucination.
- Might try periodic soft resets: micro anchor that restates role but in different words every N turns.

Example of a failure trace (hand-copied):
- Prompt (cadence-B): long thread + one anchor at top.
- Model reply: invented owner "Jordan" for an action assigned to no one.
- Post-mortem: anchor was ambiguous about "unknown owners"; exemplar pattern used names in each example so model inferred it should supply names.
- Fix applied: add explicit unknown policy to all exemplars.

Notes to self on UX for customers: 
- Offer a "cadence slider" in Console: Cheap/Default/Stable (maps to stray anchor frequency and exemplar count).
- Show token tradeoff UI: estimate tokens saved by reducing anchor frequency, estimated risk of drift (heuristic).

End-of-note quick log:
- 2024-09-12: initial experiment scaffolding + anchor phrase list created.
- 2024-10-03: noticed hallucination spike at sparse anchors.
- 2024-11-20: tried micro-anchors; promising signal.
- 2025-01-24: consolidated heuristics (this doc).

If I come back later, start by re-running cadence-A vs C on 100 CS threads and capture instruction-adherence metric explicitly (we still rely on manual judgments).

Random TODOs to migrate: create tidy PR with reproducible script + add to research/internal-benchmarks repo.

"Notes to self: keep anchor phrases short, specific, but explicit about unknowns. Try \"anchor-as-index\" if runtime KV support exists."
